SUPPLEMENTAL DECLARATION OF
ELIAS MOO
I, Elias J. Moo, pursuant to  28 U.S.C. § 1746,
hereby declare as follows:
1. I am over the age of 21 and have personal
knowledge of all contents of this declaration. I have
not been convicted of a felony or crime involving
dishonesty.
2. I am the current Superintendent of Catholic
Schools at the Archdiocese of Denver.
3. Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Denver
operates Head Start and Early Head Start programs
that serve needy families across Denver.
4. These programs are part of Catholic Charities’
ministry to the poor, serving, among others, a
significant number of families experiencing homeless
in Denver.
5. These programs are not operated as Catholic
schools in the Archdiocese, are not supervised by the
Archdiocese’s Office of Catholic Schools, do not
operate according to the Office of Catholic School’s
policies, and are not parish programs. Instead, to the
extent these programs operate in Catholic parishes in
the Archdiocese, they lease the space.
6. This charitable ministry of the Archdiocese
(like the Archdiocese’s soup kitchens and homeless
shelters) does not condition its care for the poor and
needy on adherence to Catholic beliefs or on
agreement to support and uphold Catholic teachings.
Instead, these Head Start and Early Head Start
JA 1

programs are open to all families in need, regardless
of personal circumstances, and seek to help by
providing childcare services while parents work to get
back on their feet.
7. This charitable ministry is not seeking to create
a community of believers or to provide children with a
distinctively Catholic education. Accordingly, these
Catholic Charities programs are able to sign the UPK
Program Services Agreement in good faith since they
do not, for example, prioritize Catholic families when
providing this ministry to those in need.
8. For the Archdiocese of Denver’s 36 Catholic
preschools—whose mission is  to create a Catholic
community and support parents seeking to provide
their children with a Catholic education—signing the
Agreement in good faith is not possible, as I have
explained in a prior declaration.
I declare under penalty of perjury that the
foregoing is true and correct.
Executed on October 30, 2023.

/s/ Elias J. Moo
Elias J. Moo

EXAMINATION
BY MS. RUST:
 Q. Ms. Coats, my name is Niki Rust, and I ’m an
attorney with the attorney general ’s office, and I
represent the defendants, Dr. Roy and Dawn Odean,
from the Colorado Department of Early Childhood.
 I’ ll be doing the deposition today. It ’s nice to meet
you virtually.
 Could you please identify who else is in the room
with you this morning?
 A. Joe Davis.
 Q. Okay. And then, Ms. Coats, I would ask, if you
have any chat or other type of communication open,
that you please close them. You can ’t get assistance
from anyone while answering the questions.
 So if today you need to see something or  speak to
someone when answering a question, I would ask you
just say that out loud so that we can discuss it and
make those arrangements. Okay?
 MS. RUST: And then, Mr. Davis, it ’s my
understanding that just Mr. Reaves is going to be on
the line today; is that correct?
JA 3

MR. DAVIS: Yes.

Kelly know earlier that Virginia is not with us today,
but Greg Whitehair and Janna will be joining shortly
in the room with me.
 So I can let you know, if you want, when they’re in
the room. If not, just know that they will be here.
 MR. DAVIS: Very well.
 THE REPORTER: Before we go on, Niki, did you
want to discuss exhibit numbering?

Yes, I do.
 Mr. Davis, Ms. Kelly and I were discussing whether
you wanted – if we wanted exhibits today to be

again at 1.
 My general practice is to keep them consecutive,
but I know – well, actually, we only did  one depo for

 All right. Ms. Kelly, anything else I  forgot before I
getting going?
 THE REPORTER: No. Thank you.

state and spell your full name for the record?
 A. Avery Cecile Coats, A -v-e-r-y C-e-c-i-l- e C -o-at-s.
JA 4

Coats?
 A. Yes.
 Q. What are they?

updating our room arrangements. I think she ’s

you please give your home address for the record?
 A.

 A.

know, this is going to be filed somewhere and we’ re
happy to provide the email address off the record, but
can we do that?
 MS. RUST: That’s fine, Joe.
 MR. DAVIS: Okay.
 Q. (BY MS. RUST) Okay. Ms. Coats, have you ever
been deposed before?
 A. No.
 Q. Okay. So because this is being recorded by the
court reporter, when I ask you questions, your answers
JA 5

will need to be verbal. So even though I can see you
shaking your head, you will have to give yes or no
answers.
 We also must take turns talking so that the court
reporter can get everything down and doesn’t get upset
with us. That also means that sometimes we may have
to repeat things. And I might accidentally talk over
you if I have an objection. And it ’s not meaning to be
rude. I’m just trying to insert my objection, just so you
know.
 If you need a break today, please say so. But I think
we’ll try and take a break about halfway, or every
hour, just depending on how things are going.
 But please understand that if you ask for a break,
I’ll need you to answer any pending questions before
we take a break.
 You were sworn in under oath, so we ’ll be asking
you to tell the whole truth and nothing but the truth.
And this is the same oath that is given at trial and it
should hold the same weight today; okay?
 A. (Nodded head up and down.)
 Q. I’ m here to learn everything you know about the
events and facts of this lawsuit. For that reason, I am
looking for full and complete answers to my questions.
In other words, I ’m looking for the whole truth that
you just gave an oath to give.
 Do you understand that?
 A. I understand.
 Q. Okay. You will have the opportunity to review
and change any answers given today, though if you do
JA 6

change an answer, I may ask that I be allowed to come
back here and ask you follow-up questions.
 Does that sound fair?
 A. Yes.
 Q. Thank you. If you realize that an answer you
have given is not complete or inaccurate for any
reason, will you tell me today so we can just clarify the
record?
 A. Yes.
 Q. And if I ask a question that you do not
understand, will you please tell me and I’ll do my best
to rephrase the question?
 A. Yes.
 Q. Okay. Are you on any medications today that
could affect your ability to testify?
 A. No.
 Q. Are you at all sick?
 A. No.
 Q. Is there any reason why you can’t give accurate
and complete testimony here today?
 A. No.
 Q. Okay. Before we get started, did you
understand all, kind of, my instructions?
 A. I do.

 A. John Coats, J-o-h-n.

JA 12

Q. I have a bunch of April babies in my life so

Okay. Any other dependents, Ms. Coats?

Q. Okay. Who do you report to in your role at St.

A. The pastor, Father Joe McLagan, M -c, capital

Q. Thank you. Okay. And what is your job

JA 14

faith, academics, and then our specific school

I am in charge of aligning us to our mission and

Do you want me to go into more depth?
Q. Well, that’s good for now. Thank you.

Q. Any previous employment in early childhood?
A. No.
Q. Okay. Any previous employment within a

Q. Can you describe that, please?
A. I was a long -term substitute at St. Vincent de

A. That was six weeks, and that was my

Q. Okay. Any previous employment within a

Q. Will you please describe?

JA 15

Q. And what was your job prior to principal of

Q. What is The Bradley Center?
A. It is a residential treatment facility.
Q. And what age kids did you work with there?
A. We served kids from – I think during my time
there, I believe the youngest was 6 – I could be wrong
– into early 20s.
Q. Okay. And I’m sorry. What was your role there?
I must have missed it.
A. I started as a special education teacher and
then I was the lead teacher.
Q. All right. Ms. Coats, I want to now switch and
talk about your employment through the Archdiocese
of Denver, please.
A. Yes.
Q. Would you please tell me, what is your job title
